plan_consistency: Local observed clocks and intervals, cooperative custody limits, pure/native distinction and no formal acceptance are explicit. Risks below are implementation gates, not observed implementation failures.

risks.topic: Instrument the actual transport path and broker instance exactly once
facts: RemainingTransport.operation bypasses HTTP subclass overrides by calling OpenAIResponsesHTTP methods directly for isinstance matches.
Engine execute creates its own broker via _load; it is different from a prior snapshot instance. Guard is invoked repeatedly during one step.
risks.recommendation: Use a protocol proxy rather than HTTP subclass; hook invoke only on actual broker passed to native guard, idempotently per instance. Preserve original bound callable, delegate exactly once and touch no global/class functions.
risks.bounded_test: Real HTTP-like adapter and a fake transport both produce one observed count/send; repeated guard calls do not nest broker wrappers or execute tool twice; independent broker instances remain unchanged.

risks.topic: Observation persistence must consume native timeout instead of extending it
facts: RemainingTransport computes remaining budget before passing timeout_seconds to non-HTTP transports.
Native broker recomputes context.deadline remaining before sandbox launch. Durable observer begin/end adds real elapsed work.
risks.recommendation: Fix observer forwarding deadline before journal I/O; recompute remaining after persistence and reject exhaustion before forwarding. Use the original deadline-aware HTTP bridge and leave original broker context deadline unchanged. Late effect completion does not establish cancellation.
risks.bounded_test: Artificially delayed journal begin decreases forwarded timeout; exhausted allowance delegates zero times; native context deadline remains equal; callback after fail cannot append a successful end.

risks.topic: Keep lock ordering and checkpoint CAS consistent across direct callers and crashes
facts: Public native execute acquires run lock itself and uses context.begin(expected_checkpoint) CAS.
Observation driver lock serializes participating wrappers but cannot serialize callers using the native API directly. Native context failure states never reexecute.
risks.recommendation: Use one run-lock acquisition per snapshot, release it before public execute, and never read runtime under event lock. Require exact prior/next checkpoints, cursor and global role IDs; any stale native CAS or unexplained progress closes observer uncertain. Never resume a journal left active after interrupted effect. Journal paths must be outside bound runtime and immutable input roots.
risks.bounded_test: Competing wrapper driver fails fast; direct native caller advancement causes coverage/CAS rejection; no event→run deadlock; interrupted active observation reopens uncertain; failed release on historical completed run creates no observation.

risks.topic: Expose only locally observed release-to-delivery W and valid clock-contained intervals
facts: Native send receipt monotonic timestamps surround transport invocation, including observer callbacks. Ledger send markers instead use wall time.
Native sandbox/host receipt duration has a narrower boundary than whole broker.invoke; observation overhead and pauses are inside local release-to-delivery.
risks.recommendation: Bind release to prepared cursor0/zero journals and finish to actual completed native publication plus exact D120 measurement SHA. Check same boot/declared monotonic clock, typed nonregressing ns, interval containment and all callback identities. Union same-clock intervals without double counting; keep wall deltas separate and allow wall adjustments. Label W locally observed including observation/pause overhead; outside-union time is neither human nor CPU. No W for uncertain or unfinished journal.
risks.bounded_test: Boot change and monotonic regression reject; wall regression leaves valid monotonic elapsed; overlapping intervals merge correctly; observer send interval fits its exact native receipt; tool host/sandbox remain separate; unfinished journal does not invent delivery.

risks.topic: Callback revocation, mutable results and lifecycle errors must not leak RAW or fake completeness
facts: Native batch uses daemon workers and stop flags, so callbacks can return after the controlling step has timed out.
Native execute can return an indeterminate view containing reason derived from exception text instead of propagating the original error. Payloads and returned dicts can be mutable.
risks.recommendation: Revoke step token durably on every failure or non-paused/non-completed result. Invalid/closed begin must not delegate; late end returns false without writes, including after reopen. Require final exact observed count/send/tool sets, count==ledger input, canonical response/result digests and role-specific native tool epochs. Journal stores only validated identities/hashes/numeric data/fixed error categories; never copy native reason, exception message, payload, output, tool arguments or transport credentials. Snapshot/check mutable payload/result bytes across the delegated call.
risks.bounded_test: Blocked transport completes after fail and journal bytes stay identical; paused/completed are the only successful native states; mutation/digest disagreement rejects finalization; raw/credential sentinels never appear in journal, stdout or stderr.
